sections.brief: The claim in its authors' words: Thiel 2009 Cato essay ('freedom and democracy' not compatible; 1920 franchise; 'escape from politics') and 1 May follow-up ('little hope that voting will make things better'), set against his $32m 2022 primary spending; Yarvin's Cathedral, neocameralism, 2012 'dictator phobia', NYT 2025 ('very weak', no voting, 'pornographic stimulus'), CNN 2025 'single individual'; Land ('doom itself', 'vote buying', 'No voice, free exit') with Hirschman; the shared inference and its untested premise; Federalist 10. Figures: compare (three authors), flow (the inference and the test)

Symptoms granted: Pew trust 77% (1964) to 17% (2025), Gallup confidence 48% to 28%, Pew 2026 69% dissatisfied; EIU flawed democracy since 2016 (trust cited, 7.65 in 2025), V-Dem electoral democracy 0.57, Freedom House 81; indices measure less democracy, not too much; Gilens & Page and critics; Pew 2023 money views, Citizens United 5-4/8-1, Brennan top-10 donor shares; democratisation timeline 1870-1965; the book's question; The test (incl. trust peak 1964, EIU's own cause, partisan flip). Figures: stats, compare, time
